title: Self-owned IPC namespace and POSIX mqueue backend for the android14-6.1 module
problem: src/port61 reuses the native 6.1 GKI IPC namespace and POSIX message queue objects. Device kernels that ship with CONFIG_SYSVIPC=n and CONFIG_POSIX_MQUEUE=n (so CONFIG_IPC_NS is unavailable) do not export init_ipc_ns, mq_lock, mq_init_ns, mq_clear_sbinfo, mq_put_mnt, setup_mq_sysctls or retire_mq_sysctls, and the module is rejected by simplify_symbols() with -ENOENT.
solution: Restore the self-owned IPC/mqueue design that every other port already uses (src/port515, src/port66, src/port, src/port618 all define init_ipc_ns, mq_lock, copy_ipcs, free_ipc_ns, ipcns_operations and ship their own mqueue.c/mq_sysctl.c). src/port66 is the closest template because src/port61 was derived from it.

build.make: make -j$(nproc) TARGET=namespace PORT_DIR=src/port61nomq GKI_ANDROID=android14 GKI_VERSION=6.1 OUT=/module/out/gki/android14-6.1-nomq

primary.why: the 5.15 VFS/sysctl call forms are the ones 6.1 still has: current_time(), kern_unmount(), mnt_userns, register_sysctl_table/__register_sysctl_table. src/port66 is newer than 6.1 in the places that matter (mnt_idmap, alloc_inode_sb, mnt_make_shortterm) and those symbols do not exist in a 6.1 kernel.

cross_check.why: src/port61/ORIGIN records it as the adaptation base and it carries the clearest shape of the self-owned create_ipc_ns()/mq_* lifecycle

change_list.detail: #define init_ipc_ns ds_init_ipc_ns and #define mq_lock ds_mq_lock, exactly as src/port66/names.h does
define init_ipc_ns and DEFINE_SPINLOCK(mq_lock), own copy_ipcs/free_ipc_ns/ipcns_operations/create_ipc_ns instead of importing them
module-owned init namespace handling instead of the native init_ipc_ns paths
register the module's own ipc and mqueue sysctl trees on the module-owned namespace

drop the HOOK() entries that wrap native copy_ipcs/put_ipc_ns/ipcns_put/ipcns_install, add the six mq syscall slots, and keep src/port61 KCFI-style entry checks and raw branch encodings (the device kernel is KCFI, not classic CFI)
release the module-owned namespace on task exit in the 6.1 exit path
gate on the absence of pidns_operations, ipcns_operations and any native mqueue filesystem, and on the presence of the six weak __arm64_sys_mq_* stubs
from src/port515 (5.15): current_time(), kern_unmount(), mnt_userns and register_sysctl_table all exist in 6.1; do not take src/port66 text here

from src/port515: one global /proc/sys/fs/mqueue table whose handlers rewrite table->data to the current ipc namespace. The per-namespace alternative needs the 3-argument __register_sysctl_table that src/port61/ipc_sysctl.c already uses; decide at M1
msg.c is already byte-identical to src/port66; nsproxy.c must keep the 6.1 form of copy_namespaces, not the 6.6 one

milestones.title: Own the IPC namespace and POSIX mqueue backend
exit_criteria: the new target builds clean in the 6.1 DDK
the module imports none of the blocking symbols
an offline ABI comparison of ipc_namespace/pid_namespace/pid/nsproxy against the device BTF passes

milestones.title: Representative test kernel
exit_criteria: a 6.1 test kernel built with CONFIG_SYSVIPC=n, CONFIG_POSIX_MQUEUE=n, CONFIG_PID_NS=n, CONFIG_USER_NS=n, CONFIG_DEVTMPFS=n boots in the VM harness
the repo's namespace/IPC regression suite passes on that kernel
milestones.why: the DDK kernel has native POSIX mqueue and IPC namespaces, so a VM run against it cannot prove the module works without them

milestones.title: Device load and Droidspaces smoke test
exit_criteria: ksud insmod succeeds on the device profile with no oops
created PID and IPC namespaces are real (ns ids differ, nested namespaces work)
Droidspaces starts a container with the module active
unload is refused while active and the device stays stable

milestones.title: devtmpfs and sandboxing track
exit_criteria: devtmpfs is provided for a kernel with CONFIG_DEVTMPFS=n (devtmpfs_mount and devtmpfs_create_node are absent today)
the user namespace sandboxing track is assessed against CONFIG_USER_NS=n
milestones.note: separate workstream, tracked here because Droidspaces needs it

gates.abi: scripts/abi/compare-btf.py against the device BTF for nsproxy, ipc_namespace, pid_namespace and pid
gates.vm: tests/vm harness on the M2 kernel
gates.device: ksud insmod plus the namespace checks from the device profile

open_decisions: payload selection: KMI android14-6.1 currently resolves to src/port61 for the GKI baseline and would also match this vendor profile; the installer has to pick by runtime capability check rather than by KMI alone
mqueue sysctl style: one global table (src/port515) versus a per-namespace ctl_table_set (src/port61 style)
whether the module-owned mq_init_ns/mq_clear_sbinfo/mq_put_mnt need ds_ renames to avoid clashing with a kernel that still has native POSIX mqueue (the DDK kernel does)
